newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says German tax talks to continue this week.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says German tax talks to continue this week.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday after a coalition-opposition summit on tax reforms that a further meeting would be held this week in a small group.

Waigel told reporters after three hours of talks three members from each side would meet on Friday. Wolfgang Gerhardt, leader of junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP), said he hoped for a broad agreement on tax changes by Easter.
Waigel says German tax talks to continue this week
Waigel said the coalition side would be represented at the talks by the parliamentary party leaders of the Christian Democrats (CDU) Wolfgang Schaeuble, Hermann Otto Solms of the FDP and himself.
The opposition Social Democrats (SPD) would send parliament faction chief Rudolf Scharping, North Rhine-Westphalia finance minister Heinz Schleusser and Hamburg mayor Henning Voscherau.

The two sides met on Monday for a rare tax summit to try and reach a quick deal on tax cuts to fight unemployment which in January hit 4.7 million -- the highest since 1933 -- without jeopardising efforts to qualify for European monetary union.
Waigel said Friday's talks would focus on changes to corporate taxation, saying the key element of the reform was to boost investment and job creation.
